岗哨支持

岗哨是在 iPhone 上查看自建 tesla-sentry-f50 服务器录像的客户端。

联系支持

如需 App 使用帮助，请发邮件至 support@tessyun.com，说明 App 版本、iOS 版本和遇到的情况。不要发送管理员密码、会话凭据或私人录像；截图请先遮住地址、位置和其他个人信息。回复时间视具体情况而定，暂无保证的回复时限。

1. 连接需要什么？

需要装有 iOS 18 或更高版本的 iPhone、兼容的 tesla-sentry-f50 服务器地址，以及管理员密码。地址有端口时请一并填写。不填写协议时会使用 HTTP；要使用服务器的 HTTPS，请明确填写 https://。岗哨不提供服务器，也不要求另建岗哨账号。

1.0（构建2和3）的演示仅含模拟画面；真实录像示例将随后续版本提供。

含真实录像示例的后续版本：连接页的“体验演示”可查看随 App 提供的模拟画面和一段 20 秒的真实行驶录像示例，无需连接录像服务器。

2. 为什么连接失败？

请检查地址、端口和管理员密码，确认手机能够访问服务器。连接局域网服务器时，请在 iPhone“设置”中允许岗哨使用本地网络。若提示证书问题，请检查服务器证书；App 不提供绕过证书验证的入口。HTTP 连接未加密，请只在可信网络使用，或为服务器配置 HTTPS。

3. 为什么有些读数缺失，或正在播放原画？

App 只能显示录像实际包含的数据。缺失的遥测显示“—”，不表示当时数值为零。服务器尚在准备较低清晰度的片段时，App 可能先播放原画，并显示相应提示。

4. 导出做了什么？

连接服务器时：App 请求服务器生成单分钟、单镜头的带水印视频，下载到手机后交给系统分享面板。服务器缺少水印生成条件时可能拒绝导出，请在浏览器中检查服务器。“停止等待”只结束 App 这次等待或下载；已经交给服务器的任务仍可能继续。是否保存或发送，由你在分享面板中选择。

后续版本的真实录像示例导出会复制随 App 提供的原片，保留片内署名，不额外添加水印。保存或分享仍由你选择。

5. 怎样移除已保存的服务器？

打开“服务器”，选择“返回连接页”。在“已保存的服务器”中打开该台服务器的“更多操作”菜单，选择“移除”并确认。App 会移除本机连接记录，并尝试移除保存的密码和会话。此操作不会删除服务器录像、服务器导出任务、已经完成的手机临时导出文件，以及你另存或分享的视频。服务器上的数据与访问权限需在服务器端管理。存储细节见隐私说明。

与网页查看器的差异

首次打开事件、按触发点定位时，如果触发点距本段开头不足 5 秒，岗哨从本段 0 秒开始；网页查看器在存在前一段时，会从前一段末尾开始。

触发镜头在事件中没有可用录像、而触发时刻所在片段仍有其他镜头时，岗哨使用替代镜头在触发时刻的画面作为列表封面；网页查看器回到默认封面，取默认镜头的第 1 秒画面。

Watchpost support

Watchpost is an iPhone viewer for recordings on your own tesla-sentry-f50 server.

Contact

Email support@tessyun.com for help with the app. Tell us your app version, iOS version and what happened. Do not send your admin password, session cookie or private recordings. Redact addresses, locations and other personal information from screenshots. Response times vary; no response time is guaranteed.

1. What do I need to connect?

Use an iPhone running iOS 18 or later, your compatible tesla-sentry-f50 server address, and its admin password. Include the port if your server uses one. Omitting the scheme uses HTTP; enter https:// explicitly to use your server's HTTPS. Watchpost does not provide a server or require a separate Watchpost account.

The demo in 1.0 (builds 2 and 3) contains simulated visuals only. The real recording sample will be included in a later update.

Next update with the real recording sample: On the connect screen, Try demo opens simulated visuals and a 20-second sample of real driving footage bundled with the app. No recording server connection is needed.

2. Why can't I connect?

Check the address, port and admin password. Make sure the phone can reach the server. For a server on your local network, allow Local Network for Watchpost in iPhone Settings. Check a reported certificate problem on your server; the app does not offer a way to bypass certificate checks. HTTP connections are unencrypted: use a network you trust, or configure HTTPS on your server.

3. Why are some readings missing, or playback using Original?

The app can only show data present in the recording. Missing telemetry appears as “—”; it does not mean the recorded value was zero. While your server prepares a lower-quality version, playback may use Original and say so.

4. What does export do?

When connected to your server: Export asks your server to generate one watermarked minute from one camera. It downloads the result to the phone for the system share sheet. A server without the required watermark support may refuse the export; check the server in a browser. Stop waiting ends the app's wait or download; a job already sent to the server may continue there. Saving or sending from the share sheet is your choice.

In the later update, exporting the real recording sample copies the bundled clip unchanged, keeps its on-screen credit and adds no extra watermark. You choose whether to save or share it.

5. How do I remove a saved server?

Open Servers and choose Back to connect screen. In Saved servers, open that server's More menu and choose Remove, then confirm. The app removes the local connection record and attempts to remove its saved password and session. It does not delete recordings or export jobs on the server, completed temporary export files, or videos you saved or shared elsewhere. Manage server data and access on that server. See Privacy for the storage details.

Differences from the web viewer

When an event is first opened at its trigger point and the trigger is less than five seconds into a clip, Watchpost starts at 0:00 in that clip. The web viewer starts near the end of the previous clip, if one is available.

If the triggering camera has no recording in the event but other cameras have footage in the clip containing the trigger, Watchpost uses another available camera's frame at the trigger time for the event thumbnail. The web viewer falls back to its default thumbnail, taken one second into the default camera's recording.
